newsitem.title: CANADA: Wet fields, showers slow Canadian harvest - AWP.
newsitem.headline: Wet fields, showers slow Canadian harvest - AWP.

text.p: Wet fields and spotty showers slowed wheat harvest across much of Alberta and northeastern British Columbia, the Alberta Wheat Pool said in its weekly crop report.
Harvest was 52 percent complete compared with 68 percent for the 10-year average, the report said.
"Up to three weeks of good weather would allow much of the crop to be harvested," the report said. "Grain dryers in some locations have been in operation 24 hours a day."
Hard red spring wheat was 48 percent combined against 95 percent at this time last year.
Canada Prairie spring wheat was 36 percent harvested, versus 94 percent in 1995. Soft white spring wheat harvest was 96 percent complete, ahead of last year's pace of 76 percent.
Winter wheat harvest was complete while durum wheat was 84 percent combined, mostly in line with last year's pace.
Oat harvest was 33 percent complete, well behind last year's 97 percent, and barley was 57 percent harvested against 92 percent last year.
Flax was 34 percent combined against 68 percent last year and canola was 54 percent harvested, trailing last year's pace of 96 percent.
Quality ratings, especially for wheat, continued to decline due to unfavorable harvest conditions, the report said.
